title: Six Teams, Four Spots: The IPL 2026 Playoff Race Enters Its Defining Fortnight
excerpt: RCB and Gujarat Titans sit pretty at the top, but a congested middle table means every remaining fixture could reshape the bracket.
body:
With 60 of 70 league matches played, IPL 2026 has delivered what every tournament organiser dreams of: a top two pulling clear, a volatile middle, and just enough mathematical life support to keep the bottom half interested. But as the competition enters its final ten matches, the real drama is in the fight for third and fourth — a battle that involves at least four teams and depends on results, net run rate, and no small amount of nerve.

**The top two: almost home**

Royal Challengers Bengaluru and Gujarat Titans are locked on 16 points apiece after 12 and 13 matches respectively, separated only by RCB's superior net run rate of +1.053. The defending champions have been the tournament's most consistent side, winning eight of twelve and rarely looking troubled. Gujarat, despite a 29-run defeat to Kolkata Knight Riders at Eden Gardens on May 16 — a match in which Finn Allen blasted 93 off 35 balls to power KKR to a mammoth 247/2 — remain firmly in the top two. Both are virtually certain to qualify; the remaining question is who finishes first and earns the coveted double-chance route through Qualifier 1.

**The congested middle: PBKS, SRH, RR, and CSK in a four-way scrum**

Sunrisers Hyderabad sit third on 14 points from 12 games, the only side in the chasing pack with genuine breathing room. Below them, the arithmetic turns brutal. Punjab Kings (13 points, 12 matches, one no-result) hold fourth, but Rajasthan Royals (12 points from just 11 matches) have a game in hand and a positive NRR. Chennai Super Kings, also on 12 points but with a worse run rate and all 12 matches played, are the most vulnerable of the four.

The fixture list offers little mercy. PBKS face RCB on May 17 in Mohali — a defeat would drag them back into the scrum, while a win could all but seal their passage. Rajasthan's game in hand is a double-edged sword: win it and they leapfrog Punjab; lose it and their NRR of +0.082 may not be enough to survive a tiebreaker.

**Below the line: slim margins and long odds**

Kolkata Knight Riders revived their campaign with that thumping win over Gujarat, climbing to 11 points. Sunil Narine's 2/29 and his landmark 200th match for a single IPL franchise underlined KKR's experience, but they need results elsewhere to go their way. Delhi Capitals (10 points) are all but out, and Mumbai Indians and Lucknow Super Giants — both on 8 points — have been formally eliminated.

**The diaspora watch party**

For NRI fans in the United States and Canada, the playoff race has turned early-morning streaming sessions on Willow TV and JioHotstar into appointment viewing. With time-zone-friendly afternoon matches in India starting at 6 AM Eastern, the diaspora's WhatsApp groups are buzzing with scenario calculators and NRR spreadsheets. In the UK, Sky Sports Cricket carries every match, while fans in Australia tune in via Fox Cricket. The intensity of this playoff race — with six teams still mathematically alive for four spots — has made IPL 2026 one of the most-watched seasons among overseas Indians.

**What to watch next**

The next 48 hours are pivotal. PBKS versus RCB on May 17 could either lock Punjab into the top four or blow the race wide open. With the playoffs scheduled to begin on May 26 in Dharamshala and the final set for May 31 in Ahmedabad, the league stage's remaining ten matches will determine whether the knockouts feature familiar heavyweights or a couple of gate-crashers. For fans of the sport's most lucrative league, sleep can wait.
